'guards' names the scripts that would run it. 'state' is live / dead / absent, cross-checked against disk by law_enforcement.py.

_renumber: 2026-08-23: the founder cut 32 laws to 10 ('anything that can be automated shouldn't be a law'). A check was bound to a law by its NUMBER, so the renumber silently re-pointed every check above 2 at a different law and nothing failed. Each entry now carries `was` (the number the check was written for), `law` (the number today, null if the rule retired to a machine) and `law_title` (the heading it must still match). science/map_covers_laws.py fails when a title moves out from under a check.

laws_commit.subject: laws: cut 32 to 10; retired rules become named machinery
laws_commit.why: ~/AGENTS.md is not inside any git repository, so `git log` on it shows nothing and looks frozen. The tracked copy is the snapshot, and this sha is the version every check below was written against. Recording it turns 'are the laws final?' from a question asked of a peer into a comparison a machine makes.
